passages.text: Do you ask where the Supreme Good dwells? In the soul. And unless the soul be pure and holy, there is no room in it for God.
passages.note: Where true good lives; inner purity and the sacred

passages.text: And yet the worst punishment for crime lies in the crime itself. You are mistaken, I maintain, if you propose to reserve your punishments for the hangman or the prison; the crime is punished immediately after it is committed; nay, rather, at the moment when it is committed.
passages.note: Guilt; wrongdoing punishes itself in the doing

passages.text: Those things which are goods produce confidence, but riches produce shamelessness. The things which are goods give us greatness of soul, but riches give us arrogance. And arrogance is nothing else than a false show of greatness.
passages.note: Wealth and pride; arrogance as false greatness
